description: 2 tactical challenges for Black against the Magnus Smith Trap. Never play 8...Nge7?? — strike with 8...d5! instead.

drills.briefExplanation: 8...d5! 9.exd5 exd5 10.Re1+ Be7 — break, recapture, block the check, and complete development.
drills.description: Black to play. White castled into the Morra attack — play the freeing 8...d5!.
drills.explanation: The antidote to the Magnus Smith: 8...d5! strikes in the center before White can play Ng5. After 9.exd5 exd5 10.Re1 Be7 Black completes development with a solid structure — the b4 bishop is well placed, the king is safe, and White's 'trap' never gets its Nge7?? trigger. Against gambits, central counterplay beats passive defense.
drills.name: The d5 Break

drills.briefExplanation: 9...d5! 10.exd5 Nxd5 — meet the knight lunge with the central break.
drills.description: Black to play. White lunged 9.Ng5 — find the only defense.
drills.explanation: The critical defensive try after 9.Ng5: 9...d5! opens the center while White's knight is offside. After 10.exd5 Nxd5 Black's knight lands centrally with tempo, the e6 pawn's weakness is covered, and White's attack evaporates — the g5 knight will have to retreat, losing time. One accurate break defuses the whole trap.
drills.name: Defusing Ng5
